title: Run a useful AI SEO audit on three real store pages
description: An AI SEO audit is useful when it produces a small set of evidence-backed changes. Start with a homepage, a category and a product you actually sell, rather than asking a tool to invent hundreds of recommendations.
body:
An AI SEO audit is useful when it produces a small set of evidence-backed changes. Start with a homepage, a category and a product you actually sell, rather than asking a tool to invent hundreds of recommendations.

## Define the decision before collecting suggestions

Write down what is wrong or unknown. Perhaps customers search for a product but land on an unrelated page. Perhaps the product title omits its defining size. Perhaps the category introduction makes a delivery promise the shop cannot honour. These are different problems and should not become one generic SEO score.

Give the tool the visible page content and the task you want the visitor to complete. Remove customer details, private dashboards and credentials. A public-page audit does not need an order export.

## Ask for evidence attached to every recommendation

Request the exact existing phrase, the proposed change, the reason and the fact that supports it. Reject a recommendation that cannot identify its source. A tool that says to add free shipping because competitors mention it has not discovered a business capability.

Google's people-first guidance emphasises useful, reliable content rather than writing primarily to manipulate rankings. It also says Google has no preferred word count. Use that as a boundary, not a claim that one particular article length will perform best. [Google Search Central](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content)

## Separate editorial fixes from technical work

A clearer heading may be a content edit. A missing canonical, inaccessible page or broken redirect needs technical investigation. Do not accept generated code changes just because they accompany reasonable copy advice.

Create three queues: facts to verify, text to improve and implementation to investigate. Assign an owner to each. The person who knows the product should confirm the material and delivery claims; the person maintaining the site should assess the technical change.

## Use one product as a controlled example

Imagine a handmade pouch page titled simply “New collection.” A better title may identify the pouch and its actual material. The audit should not add waterproof, organic or same-day delivery unless those claims are supported.

Keep a before copy, make the smallest useful revision and check the mobile page. Confirm the product options and buying link still work. A change that improves a title while removing the size explanation is not an overall improvement.

## Decide how you will judge the result

Record the date, changed fields and page. Compare relevant search queries and customer questions over a meaningful period. Do not attribute every movement to the edit when promotions, stock or seasonality also changed.

A completed audit leaves fewer unexplained recommendations, not a larger spreadsheet. Start with three pages, resolve the facts and expand the method only when it helps you make better decisions. Use the [guide library](/guides/) to address the underlying catalogue or customer-service problem when SEO is only the symptom.

## Illustrative case to check

Suppose the three pages are a homepage, a pouch category and a small cotton pouch. The audit proposes “same-day dispatch” on all three, but the merchant only confirms that service for ready stock. Hold that claim rather than applying it everywhere. Accept a factual product-name correction separately. Your result log should show one accepted edit and one unresolved operating claim, not a single percentage score that hides the difference.

title: Rewrite a product page title around the promise it can keep
description: A product title should identify the page clearly enough that the right buyer understands why it is relevant. Adding every possible search phrase can make that job harder rather than easier.
body:
A product title should identify the page clearly enough that the right buyer understands why it is relevant. Adding every possible search phrase can make that job harder rather than easier.

## Start with the actual product identity

Write the product type, the distinguishing attribute and the brand only where it helps. Decide which difference matters to the customer: size, material, intended use or a specific range. Do not choose an attribute merely because a keyword tool gives it a large number.

For an illustrated example, “Cotton drawstring gift pouch, small” tells a buyer more than “Best premium shopping gift product online.” The first still needs to be true: the material and size must match the listing.

## Keep the title and visible heading coherent

The title field and the main page heading serve related purposes. They need not be mechanically identical, but they should not describe different products or offers. Check category templates that accidentally reuse one title across many pages.

Google explains that title links can be generated from several page signals, not only the title element you write. It recommends descriptive, concise titles and avoiding repetitive boilerplate. Your edit does not guarantee an exact search-result display. [Google title-link guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/title-link)

## Remove claims that require missing evidence

Words such as certified, fastest, official or best can imply more than the page proves. A sale amount can also become stale. Prefer a stable product identity unless you have a reliable process for maintaining the changing information.

Ask an AI tool to suggest alternatives only from verified facts. Give it a forbidden-claims list as well as the product description. Reject an attractive title if it silently invents a material, audience or delivery benefit.

## Check the page family, not just one item

Review a category page and several product titles together. Can a shopper distinguish them? Are two near-identical products really separate pages, or are they options of one product? A title edit cannot solve a confused catalogue structure.

Keep a simple register with current title, proposed title, reason and checked facts. That makes a later correction possible without guessing what was changed or why.

## Test the whole customer-facing result

Open the page on mobile after saving. Confirm the heading, selected product and navigation still make sense. Then inspect the relevant search information over time without promising an immediate ranking change.

The useful outcome is a clearer promise to the appropriate visitor. If a title attracts a click by describing something the page does not supply, it has created a new problem. Pair this work with [catalogue guidance](/guides/catalogue-and-stock/) before multiplying the same mistake across the store.

## Illustrative case to check

Consider two products: a small cotton pouch and a large linen pouch. Giving both the title “Premium gift bag” makes them difficult to distinguish. Draft titles using the verified material and size, then inspect the actual product pages. If the small item is sold as a pair, include that fact where it affects the buying decision. Do not add “eco-friendly” merely because the material sounds natural.

title: Write a search description that helps the right visitor choose
description: A search description should explain what the page offers, not repeat a string of disconnected keywords. Treat it as a short, accurate invitation to a page that already answers a useful question.
body:
A search description should explain what the page offers, not repeat a string of disconnected keywords. Treat it as a short, accurate invitation to a page that already answers a useful question.

## Identify the page's job

A product page, a delivery guide and a comparison article need different descriptions. The product helps someone evaluate an item. The delivery guide answers a practical concern. The comparison explains a decision and its limits.

Write the one sentence a reader should understand before clicking. If that sentence is vague, improve the page's purpose before polishing its metadata.

## Use specific information without overpromising

A useful description can mention the actual subject, the decision covered and an important boundary. For example, a guide about direct payment can explain that it distinguishes placing an order from confirming receipt. It should not promise instant settlement if the process is manual.

Keep temporary prices and deadlines out unless the field is maintained with the same care as the visible page. A stale description can attract someone with an offer that no longer exists.

## Understand what the field controls

Google may use a page's meta description when it is useful, but it can also generate a snippet from page content for a query. Writing the field is not a guarantee that every search result uses your exact sentence. [Google snippet guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/snippet)

That makes the visible page important. Do not hide the useful answer in metadata while leaving the main text generic or contradictory.

## Use AI for alternatives, not missing facts

Provide the page text and ask for three descriptions aimed at its actual reader. Require each version to avoid unverified benefits, rankings and urgency. Choose the one that best matches the page, then check it manually.

Do not ask a tool to copy a competitor's description and replace the company name. The competitor may have different features, terms or intent. Original wording should come from your own page's purpose.

## Review duplicates and the next action

Read several descriptions together. Reusing a broad company slogan on every product makes the pages harder to distinguish. At the same time, do not manufacture differences between duplicate pages solely to make the metadata look unique.

After a visitor clicks, the page should make its next step obvious: read a relevant section, inspect a product option or follow a related guide. A description is part of that sequence, not an isolated ranking trick.

Keep the revision date and compare outcomes cautiously. Search demand and the mix of queries can change independently of the wording. Use the [store design and choice hub](/guides/choosing-and-designing-store/) when the larger problem is a mismatch between the visitor's expectation and the page.

## Illustrative case to check

A delivery guide explains standard delivery, an optional fast request and locations the shop cannot serve. Its description should preview those topics, not say “Fast delivery everywhere.” The test is simple: after reading the description and opening the page, would the visitor feel accurately guided? Keep the important restriction visible in the page itself, because the search engine may choose a different excerpt.

title: Check product structured data against the page a customer sees
description: Product structured data should describe the real page and offer. Before asking someone to add markup, make sure the visible product, price, availability and option handling are consistent.
body:
Product structured data should describe the real page and offer. Before asking someone to add markup, make sure the visible product, price, availability and option handling are consistent.

## Begin with the customer-facing record

Choose an ordinary product and one with a meaningful variation. Record what a buyer sees before and after selecting an option. A product-wide starting price and a selected-variant price can be different, so the implementation needs to represent that deliberately.

Do not use an old catalogue export as unquestioned truth. If the live price changed yesterday, a technically valid block of stale data can still be wrong.

## Understand the purpose without expecting a reward

Google documents product structured data for product-related search experiences, with different guidance for product snippets and merchant listings. Eligibility and valid markup do not guarantee a particular appearance in results. [Google product guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/product)

Ask the implementer which experience the page is intended to support and which current requirements apply. Avoid copying a random code example without matching it to the page's actual type.

## Make a field comparison sheet

Compare product identity, URL, image, currency, price, availability and any review information used. For every field, write where it comes from and when it updates. A value entered twice by hand is a maintenance risk.

The sheet should also identify who notices failures. If a stock change updates the page but not the structured data, the store needs an observable correction path, not a promise that it normally works.

## Test difficult states deliberately

Inspect a sale ending, an unavailable item, a deleted product and a variant change. Use a controlled environment or an authorised existing example; do not alter live stock solely to obtain a screenshot.

A successful validation tool result is one check, not the entire test. Also compare the rendered page and the actual buying choice. Keep screenshots and the tested URL with the date so a later discrepancy can be investigated.

## Avoid invented review evidence

Do not add an aggregate rating from a handful of unrelated testimonials or generate reviews to complete a schema example. Product reviews should belong to the product and retain their provenance.

Finish with a named source for each field and a regression check for changes. This is an implementation brief, not a claim that every oBizee deployment already exposes every form of markup. Use [catalogue guidance](/guides/catalogue-and-stock/) to fix the underlying product record before adding another representation of it.

## Illustrative case to check

A product page shows a starting price of ₹500, while the selected large option costs ₹700. Check which offer the markup describes and whether its URL leads to the matching choice. Do not force both amounts to ₹500 to pass a superficial comparison. Record the selection state and the intended representation, then ask the implementer to demonstrate the rule on another option.

title: Separate product-review stars from general store praise
description: A customer saying they enjoyed buying from your shop is not automatically reviewing every product in the catalogue. Keep the subject of a review clear before displaying or marking up a rating.
body:
A customer saying they enjoyed buying from your shop is not automatically reviewing every product in the catalogue. Keep the subject of a review clear before displaying or marking up a rating.

## Identify exactly what was reviewed

The review might concern a product, delivery experience, service or the business overall. Retain that distinction. Moving general praise onto a specific product can create an impression the customer never intended.

Record the source, date, reviewed item and any permission needed for reuse. If the reviewer discussed several products together, do not silently split the statement into multiple apparently independent reviews.

## Keep display and search eligibility separate

A visible testimonial and a search-result rating are different matters. Google has specific review-snippet rules and supported types, and valid structured data does not guarantee a rich result. [Review-snippet documentation](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/review-snippet)

Ask an implementer to evaluate the correct subject and current requirements. Do not assume that adding stars to a page qualifies the business for stars in search.

## Preserve the meaning when shortening text

An excerpt should not remove the condition that changes the review's meaning. “Lovely colour, but smaller than expected” cannot honestly become only “Lovely” beside a claim about perfect sizing.

If the display needs less text, use an accurate excerpt with a route to the fuller context where appropriate. Do not invent a rating when the original feedback contained no numerical score.

## Review the aggregation method

Write down which reviews are included in an average and why. Check how duplicates, removed products and imported records are treated. A rounded display should not become a different underlying score.

For a small shop, a few genuine reviews with clear context can be more useful than a large unexplained rating. Do not fill an empty state with fictional customers or transfer feedback from a different merchant.

## Choose a trustworthy next step

Start with one product's evidence. Confirm that the displayed text and score can be traced back to the original record, then examine how a new review enters the system. Keep moderation focused on relevance, abuse and policy rather than removing every criticism.

This is a review-governance decision as much as a design task. Use the [customer-service library](/guides/fulfilment-and-support/) to prepare responses and follow-up, and treat any proposed search appearance as conditional rather than a promised outcome.

## Illustrative case to check

A customer writes “Helpful seller; the replacement arrived safely” without rating a particular item. That can be genuine business feedback, but assigning it as a five-star product review invents both a score and a subject. Keep the statement in its appropriate context or ask through a legitimate feedback process. An empty product-rating state is more honest than a completed-looking one built from unrelated praise.

title: Prepare review records for a store move without losing their origin
description: Moving reviews is not just transferring text into a new template. Preserve the evidence that connects each review to its source, product and original context.
body:
Moving reviews is not just transferring text into a new template. Preserve the evidence that connects each review to its source, product and original context.

## Export before editing

Keep an untouched copy of the source export in an appropriately private location. Record the export date and the system it came from. Work on a separate copy so a transformation mistake does not destroy the only available evidence.

Do not upload a complete customer dataset when the review migration needs only a narrower set of fields. Inspect the export for email addresses, order identifiers and attachments that should not become public.

## Map the product relationship

Create a mapping between the old product reference and the new one. Titles alone are weak identifiers because names can change or be reused. A review of an old material or discontinued version may need context rather than attachment to the latest product.

For an illustrated case, two products called “Classic pouch” may differ in size and fabric. Similar wording is not enough to prove their reviews are interchangeable.

## Retain important provenance

Keep the original date, text, rating if one existed, source reference and relevant verification status. Do not turn every imported review into a newly verified purchase. The destination's labels should reflect what the migration can actually prove.

If a field cannot be imported, decide how its meaning will be preserved or whether the review should be withheld. Silently dropping a qualification is not a harmless formatting change.

## Test a deliberately awkward sample

Include a long review, a review without a rating, a duplicate, an edited product and a record with a photo. Check the public display and the private stored values. Use authorised data and avoid making a test import visible to customers.

The test should establish how to undo or correct the import. Re-running a file must not be assumed safe unless the tool's duplicate handling has been demonstrated.

## Reconcile before opening the new page

Compare accepted, rejected and withheld counts with the source. Investigate differences rather than celebrating a matching total that may contain duplicates. Keep the old-to-new mapping and the import result together.

This guide does not claim that oBizee has a review-import integration. Confirm the actual tool and supported format before preparing a live migration. Read [platform evaluation guidance](/guides/choosing-and-designing-store/) to include evidence portability in a broader store move.

## Illustrative case to check

An export contains 80 records: 65 map clearly, ten concern discontinued products and five have uncertain references. A defensible first import may contain only the 65 clear records. Preserve the other 15 with reasons and investigate them separately. Do not change their product IDs until the total reaches 80 merely to make the migration appear complete.

title: Match imported reviews to the right product version
description: A review can remain authentic while becoming misleading on the wrong product page. Product mapping deserves its own check, especially when sizes, materials or editions have changed.
body:
A review can remain authentic while becoming misleading on the wrong product page. Product mapping deserves its own check, especially when sizes, materials or editions have changed.

## Define the identity rule

Decide what makes two records the same reviewed product. A stable product reference is a useful starting point, but a materially changed item may still need a version distinction. Do not let a matching title decide the question automatically.

Write the rule before importing. Otherwise each ambiguous row becomes an improvised judgement made under deadline pressure.

## Separate options from replacements

A colour option may belong to one product family; a redesigned construction may be a replacement. The correct treatment depends on what the review actually describes. A comment about fit or durability can be especially sensitive to a version change.

Keep an explicit unresolved group when the evidence is insufficient. It is better to hold a review than to assign it confidently to the wrong item.

## Build a mapping with reasons

For each old reference, record the destination, the basis for the match and any display note required. Use a second field for ambiguous or withheld records rather than overloading a blank destination.

An illustrative row might say that the original and destination share the same SKU and dimensions, while another is withheld because the material changed. Those reasons make future corrections easier.

## Check the rendered context

Inspect the destination product alongside the review. Does the review refer to an option no longer available? Does the photograph show a previous version? Does a shortened excerpt remove the clue that would explain the difference?

Do not treat successful file ingestion as successful editorial migration. A technically accepted row can still tell the wrong story.

## Close with reconciliation and ownership

Count mapped, withheld and rejected records, and name the person responsible for unresolved cases. Preserve the original export privately. If you later correct a mapping, keep the reason rather than overwriting the history without explanation.

For a small catalogue, reviewing every ambiguous record may be practical. For a larger one, automate the obvious matches but keep a human decision for uncertain identity. The aim is not maximum imported volume; it is reliable evidence on the page where a customer uses it.

Use the [catalogue hub](/guides/catalogue-and-stock/) to stabilise product references before beginning a review move. No particular review app or platform capability is assumed by this process.

## Illustrative case to check

A pouch changed from a zip closure to a drawstring version while keeping a similar name. A review praising the zip should not silently appear as evidence for the new closure. Keep the older version distinct or retain an explicit, accurate context if the system supports it. The mapping decision should follow the reviewed product, not the convenience of the new catalogue.

title: Choose a review-request moment that reflects the real order state
description: Ask for feedback after the customer has had a fair chance to experience the product. A fixed delay from checkout can be inappropriate when production, delivery or a service appointment is still pending.
body:
Ask for feedback after the customer has had a fair chance to experience the product. A fixed delay from checkout can be inappropriate when production, delivery or a service appointment is still pending.

## Identify the experience you want reviewed

Product use, delivery service and the buying process are different subjects. If you ask about the product before it arrives, the customer can only comment on expectations or communication.

State the subject clearly. A short request about the received item is more useful than a vague demand for a five-star rating.

## Use an actual completion signal

Decide which record establishes that the relevant experience happened. For a parcel, that might involve a reliable delivery state and a reasonable opportunity to inspect the item. For a service, it may be completion rather than the booking date.

Do not assume every platform status is independently verified. If your workflow updates delivery manually, the review routine inherits that limitation.

## Exclude unresolved exceptions

An order under investigation needs assistance, not an automatic rating request. Build a way to hold requests for unresolved non-delivery, cancellations or an incorrect item. That does not mean suppressing criticism; it means addressing the problem before sending an irrelevant message.

Keep the eventual feedback route open. A customer who experienced a problem should not become permanently ineligible to describe it.

## Write a neutral request

Ask for an honest account of the product and make the next action clear. Avoid suggested praise, prefilled positive wording or pressure linked to support. Do not promise a reward that requires a favourable score.

An illustrative structure is: identify the order privately, ask whether the customer has used the item, invite genuine feedback and provide a support route for unresolved issues. Adapt it to the communication permission and channel you actually have.

## Measure usefulness, not just response volume

Track whether requests reach the right stage, whether customers understand them and whether the resulting feedback answers future buyers' questions. A larger number of low-context ratings is not necessarily more useful.

Review a small sample of recent orders before automating. Record the rule, exceptions and owner. This guide does not assume a built-in review-request integration or permission to message every past customer.

Use the [fulfilment and support hub](/guides/fulfilment-and-support/) to align the request with your real order process, then evaluate a tool against that process rather than adopting its default schedule unquestioned.

## Illustrative case to check

One order is delivered, another is still being made and a third has an unresolved wrong-item complaint. A single “seven days after purchase” message would reach three different experiences. Review the actual states, hold the inappropriate requests and address the complaint. The rule should describe the experience being reviewed, with an exception path, rather than hiding dissatisfaction by excluding the customer forever.

title: Choose a store domain you can continue to control
description: A domain decision includes ownership, access and renewal—not just a memorable name. Choose an address your business can keep using when a contractor, platform or team member changes.
body:
A domain decision includes ownership, access and renewal—not just a memorable name. Choose an address your business can keep using when a contractor, platform or team member changes.

## Separate the name from the account

A suitable name is only part of the decision. Establish which account registers it, who can recover that account and how renewal is handled. Do not leave the only access with someone whose involvement may be temporary.

Record the registrar and renewal date without putting passwords into a shared planning document. Use the provider's authorised access controls rather than casually sharing one login.

## Test the name in ordinary conversation

Read it aloud, type it from memory and ask whether the spelling is easy to explain. Consider whether it still fits the business if the catalogue grows. Avoid assuming a domain's availability proves you have rights to use a brand name.

This guide is not a trademark assessment. Resolve naming-rights concerns through an appropriate process before spending on packaging or promotion.

## Compare the continuing cost

Look beyond the introductory offer. Record the renewal price, included services and any separate email or privacy costs relevant to your purchase. Use the [plan-cost calculator](/resources/plan-cost/) for your own quoted figures, not as a source of registrar prices.

A cheap first year can be reasonable, but it should be a deliberate choice rather than a surprise at renewal.

## Keep platform connection separate from ownership

Before buying through a website provider, ask how the domain can be managed or moved later. Request the actual process and any restrictions that apply to your account. Do not treat a marketing phrase such as free domain as a complete explanation of control.

Also identify which hostnames serve the shop, email and any existing application. A future storefront change should not begin with a guess about what the address already supports.

## Make a small ownership record

Keep the business owner, authorised operators, recovery route, renewal responsibility and intended use together. Review it when staff or suppliers change.

Then choose the name. The result should be an address that is clear to customers and maintainable by the business. Use the [platform-choice hub](/guides/choosing-and-designing-store/) to evaluate the surrounding store workflow without assuming domain registration includes hosting, email or migration assistance.

## Illustrative case to check

A freelancer registers the domain while building the shop. Before launch, establish the business's authorised ownership and recovery arrangement, who pays renewal and how the freelancer's access is managed. Do not solve this by placing the password in a shared spreadsheet. The handover is complete when the business can maintain the address through the provider's proper process.

title: Prepare a custom-domain cutover before changing any record
description: A custom-domain cutover is a change to an existing service boundary. Write the destination, current state and rollback before editing DNS or a hosting association.
body:
A custom-domain cutover is a change to an existing service boundary. Write the destination, current state and rollback before editing DNS or a hosting association.

## Identify what already serves the address

Record the exact hostname, the current provider and any related services. A screenshot of one DNS row is not a complete dependency map. Include the hosting-side association and certificate status as well as the zone record.

Do not assume that a new storefront has permission to replace every subdomain of a merchant's domain.

## Verify the destination independently

Check the new build on an appropriate protected or temporary address before directing customer traffic to it. Verify the intended merchant, assets, product routes and backend connection. A successful homepage build does not prove checkout or order lookup works.

Keep test activity read-only unless real transactions are explicitly authorised. Do not create customer orders merely to make a launch checklist green.

## Define the exact change

Write which record or association will be created or changed, who will do it and what must remain untouched. Include email-related and unrelated application records in the preservation boundary.

Avoid giving a generic DNS command without the provider's actual instructions. The required record depends on the hosting setup; an example from another store is not a safe substitute.

## Prepare rollback as an operation

Record the previous values and the conditions that trigger reversal. Distinguish reversing traffic from undoing data written after launch. Moving a hostname back does not automatically erase orders or restore a database.

Assign an observer who can check both the new storefront and any service that must remain available. Include the certificate and customer-facing routes, not just whether a name resolves.

## Close only after the real hostname works

Check the live address after the change and record the observed result. Allow for the actual provider and resolver behaviour without promising an exact universal propagation time.

If URLs change, search continuity needs its own mapping and monitoring. Google's migration guidance separates preparation, URL mapping, redirects and observation. [Google site-move guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes)

Use the [store evaluation guides](/guides/choosing-and-designing-store/) to ensure the destination is ready before the domain becomes the next avoidable emergency.

## Illustrative case to check

A shop already uses its main domain for marketing and a separate hostname for orders. The new storefront is intended for only one address. Write that exact boundary and preserve the other service. A successful new build does not authorise replacing a wildcard or the entire zone. Have the operator confirm the smallest required change and retain evidence of both services before and after it.

title: Protect business email while connecting a new storefront domain
description: A storefront change should not casually replace the configuration that keeps business email working. Treat the domain as shared infrastructure even when the immediate task concerns only the shop.
body:
A storefront change should not casually replace the configuration that keeps business email working. Treat the domain as shared infrastructure even when the immediate task concerns only the shop.

## Inventory the services before editing

List the website, email provider and any other applications using the domain. Ask the authorised operator to identify the records and provider settings supporting them. Do not infer that every unfamiliar entry is obsolete.

The inventory should contain record names and purposes, not account passwords or secret recovery information.

## Ask for the smallest required change

Use the storefront host's exact instructions for the intended hostname. If the proposed action replaces nameservers or imports a whole zone, stop and account for every existing service first. A one-record connection and a zone migration are not the same task.

Do not follow an instruction for another merchant's domain just because the platform name is the same.

## Keep a readable before-state

Retain an authorised export or record of the relevant configuration and who captured it. Record the email provider's current setup separately so a later issue can be compared with evidence rather than memory.

Protect that file appropriately. Some configuration details are public, but the surrounding account information may not be.

## Test the services that must survive

Plan a website check and an authorised email send-and-receive check using appropriate business test accounts. Do not use a customer's inbox as a diagnostic tool.

A page loading successfully is not evidence that mail still works. Conversely, an email delay should be investigated without immediately reversing unrelated storefront changes.

## Keep ownership clear after launch

Name who handles domain renewal, email-provider administration and hosting changes. If different people own those tasks, document the handoff so the next change is not made in isolation.

This article is a preservation checklist, not provider-specific DNS instructions. Ask the relevant providers to confirm their required records and use an authorised operator for changes. The [domain and platform decision guides](/guides/choosing-and-designing-store/) help separate the services you are buying before a low-cost website offer becomes an unexpected email migration.

## Illustrative case to check

A hosting guide suggests changing nameservers, but the domain also carries the business mailbox. Treat that as a broader migration requiring the existing mail configuration, not as a routine storefront step. Ask whether a narrower connection is supported. If the broader change is necessary, include authorised mail checks and a complete preservation plan before any edit.

title: Map old product links before moving a store
description: A store move can leave useful product links behind in search, messages, QR codes and social posts. Map those destinations before the old site disappears.
body:
A store move can leave useful product links behind in search, messages, QR codes and social posts. Map those destinations before the old site disappears.

## Collect links from more than the menu

Start with important product and category URLs, then include pages shared in campaigns, support messages and packaging. A navigation menu rarely contains every address a customer can still reach.

Keep images and downloadable documents in scope when customers or other sites link to them. Record the old URL and its purpose before deciding the destination.

## Choose the closest genuine replacement

A moved product should lead to the corresponding product where one exists. Do not send every old URL to the new homepage merely because it is convenient. For discontinued items, decide what honest customer-facing state is appropriate.

The mapping should identify merged, removed and unchanged pages separately. That prevents a missing product from being silently treated as a successful migration.

## Give the implementer a testable table

Include old URL, intended new URL, expected response and owner. Add a reason for ambiguous cases. Keep the list stable enough to test before launch and after cutover.

Google's site-move documentation recommends preparing a URL mapping and monitoring the old and new URLs. Search changes can fluctuate during a move; no table guarantees immediate traffic continuity. [Google migration guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes)

## Test the destination content

A redirect reaching a page is not sufficient if that page describes the wrong item. Inspect the selected product, images and buying options. Check a few links from the actual social or messaging context where customers use them.

Avoid testing only the homepage. A successful root URL can coexist with dozens of broken deep links.

## Keep the old evidence available

Retain the mapping, test results and relevant before-state. If a valuable link fails later, the team should know what it was intended to do. Do not delete the old records immediately after the first successful smoke test.

Use the [catalogue hub](/guides/catalogue-and-stock/) to resolve product identity before the move. Link preservation is not a separate SEO decoration; it is part of helping an existing customer find the thing they already intended to buy.

## Illustrative case to check

An old campaign links to a floral scarf that now has a different URL. Map it to that scarf, not to an unrelated new collection. Another old item is permanently discontinued; record that separately and choose an honest destination or unavailable response. The mapping table should explain both cases so the implementer does not apply one blanket redirect.

title: Create a search baseline before rewriting the whole catalogue
description: A search baseline should describe the data you actually have. Approximate weekly impressions and clicks are useful, but they cannot reveal every query, conversion or customer segment.
body:
A search baseline should describe the data you actually have. Approximate weekly impressions and clicks are useful, but they cannot reveal every query, conversion or customer segment.

## Write the scope beside the number

Record the source, date range, property and any filters. If the numbers are an estimate supplied by the business, label them as such. Do not present them as an independently verified analytics export.

For example, approximately 120 clicks from 5,000 impressions gives a ratio of about 2.4%. That arithmetic does not establish a purchase conversion rate or explain why any particular page was clicked.

## Separate page visibility from business outcomes

Search impressions and clicks answer a different question from completed orders. A customer may visit from search, return through a message and order later. Without the relevant measurement, do not assign the sale to the last page you edited.

Google describes Search Console as a tool for monitoring search performance and diagnosing aspects of a site's presence in Search. Use the reports available to the authorised property rather than inventing missing detail. [Search Console introduction](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/monitor-debug/search-console-start)

## Save a small, useful comparison set

Choose the pages you intend to change and retain their available baseline. Include query context where you have it, but keep the absence of data explicit. A screenshot of top pages is not a full query export.

Note promotions, stock changes and seasonality that may affect interpretation. The comparison is stronger when you know what else changed.

## Set a narrow first question

Ask whether a specific page now attracts more relevant visits or answers the customer's question more clearly. Avoid changing titles, navigation, offers and the entire catalogue at once if you want to learn which problem was solved.

A small site can still make sensible improvements without perfect analytics. Fix demonstrably incorrect content while keeping performance claims modest.

## Review without declaring victory too early

Choose an observation period appropriate to the traffic and change. Do not invent a universal number of days that proves success. Look for consistent evidence and investigate surprising movements.

Use the [growth and selling hub](/guides/selling-online/) to connect the search work to the actual buying journey. A baseline is valuable because it limits what you can honestly conclude, not because it supplies a flattering chart.

## Illustrative case to check

Your only evidence is a weekly estimate of 5,000 impressions and 120 clicks plus a list of top pages. Keep those as the baseline and label the missing query and order data. You can still correct a misleading title, but you cannot claim that the edit increased sales by a particular percentage without the relevant measurement.

title: Define a purchase event before installing another marketing tag
description: Before adding a pixel or analytics tag, decide what your business means by purchase. A submitted request, created order, successful payment and delivered order are not interchangeable events.
body:
Before adding a pixel or analytics tag, decide what your business means by purchase. A submitted request, created order, successful payment and delivered order are not interchangeable events.

## Draw the business sequence

Write the steps your store actually follows. A direct-payment order may exist before the merchant confirms receipt. A gateway flow may create an order before payment completes. A service request may still need acceptance.

Choose the event that each report is intended to count. Do not use a convenient button click as a substitute for a confirmed business outcome.

## Specify the fields and their sources

Identify the order reference, amount, currency and product information that the event should carry. Record whether the amount includes shipping, discounts or tax. A number without its definition cannot be reconciled reliably.

Google Analytics documents recommended ecommerce events and their parameters. Use the current provider specification for the system you implement; this article is not an event-code recipe. [GA4 event reference](https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/collection/ga4/reference/events)

## Test unsuccessful paths too

A cancelled payment, validation failure or repeated page load should not accidentally count as a new completed purchase. Ask the implementer to demonstrate those cases in a controlled environment.

Do not create live charges or real customer records without authorisation. A test should prove the event boundary without becoming an unwanted business transaction.

## Keep the reporting meaning visible

Name reports in a way that matches the event. If you measure order requests, call them requests. Calling them paid purchases can make campaign performance look better while hiding the collection work still required.

Also distinguish platform-reported attribution from the business's order ledger. They can differ for reasons that need investigation rather than automatic correction.

## Install only after the definition is agreed

Give the implementer the event definition, allowed data and negative cases. Confirm privacy and consent requirements through the appropriate process before collecting visitor information.

The result should be one coherent measurement plan, not several tags each counting a different milestone as revenue. Use the [order-workspace overview](/features/order-workspace/) to keep the operational state distinct from marketing measurement. No native integration is assumed by this guide.

## Illustrative case to check

A direct-payment customer submits an order and transfers funds later. If your report counts submission as paid revenue, it overstates what has been confirmed at that moment. Define separate milestones or label the existing event as an order request. The event plan should match the real business state, even if that makes the dashboard less immediately impressive.

title: Check browser and server event duplicates before trusting campaign revenue
description: Sending an event from both a browser and a server can produce misleading totals if the implementation does not identify the same business event consistently. Ask for a duplicate test before using the report to increase spending.
body:
Sending an event from both a browser and a server can produce misleading totals if the implementation does not identify the same business event consistently. Ask for a duplicate test before using the report to increase spending.

## Start with one real event identity

Define which order or payment outcome the event represents. Then identify the stable reference both delivery paths should use. A new random identifier on every retry may describe delivery attempts rather than the underlying purchase.

The exact deduplication mechanism depends on the receiving platform. Require the implementer to use its current documentation rather than assuming all providers use the same fields.

## Separate retries from new business activity

A network retry is not another order. A thank-you-page reload is not another payment. A second product purchase genuinely is a different event. Put those cases into the acceptance test.

The test should check the provider's received result as well as the local code. A console message saying sent does not establish how the report counted it.

## Reconcile a controlled sample

Use authorised test events or a safe test environment. Record the expected business outcomes, the browser sends, the server sends and the resulting counted events. Keep personal information out of the evidence.

If two sends produce one counted purchase, retain that proof. If they produce two, fix the identity or event-boundary problem before scaling campaigns.

## Check amounts independently

Duplicate prevention does not establish that the revenue amount is correct. Compare currency and the treatment of delivery, discounts and refunds with the reporting definition.

A dashboard can have the correct event count and still report a misleading value. Do not let one successful test stand in for the entire measurement contract.

## Own the ongoing check

Record who maintains the integration and what changes should trigger a re-test. Checkout changes, new payment paths and tag-manager edits can all affect the event boundary.

This guide does not claim oBizee has every browser/server integration or that a particular provider guarantees exact attribution. Use the [campaign budget tool](/resources/campaign-budget/) only after the contribution and order assumptions behind your spending decision are understood.

## Illustrative case to check

In a test, one order produces a browser send and a server send, followed by a retry of the server request. The expected business count is still one if all three represent the same outcome. Record the provider result and identifiers using its documented mechanism. If the total becomes three, stop using that report for spending decisions until the implementation is corrected.

title: Keep catalogue-feed identifiers stable across product changes
description: A product feed needs a reliable way to identify the item it describes. Treat identifiers as a data contract rather than rebuilding them from whatever title happens to be visible today.
body:
A product feed needs a reliable way to identify the item it describes. Treat identifiers as a data contract rather than rebuilding them from whatever title happens to be visible today.

## Distinguish a product family from a sellable option

A parent product and a particular size or colour can require different representations. Decide how the feed, storefront and marketing events refer to the same sellable item.

Do not assume that matching display names establish identity. Names can change, and two products can share similar wording.

## Record the mapping explicitly

Keep the internal product reference, any variant reference, destination URL and external feed identifier together. Write down what happens when a product is renamed, removed or replaced.

Google Merchant Center's product data specification defines identifiers and product attributes for its feeds. Check the current rules for the destination you use rather than transferring one platform's format to another. [Merchant Center specification](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/7052112?hl=en)

## Test a rename and a variant

Use a controlled sample to see whether a title change accidentally creates a new item. Check that a selected variant opens the relevant buying choice and reports the appropriate price and availability.

A feed accepted without errors can still point to the wrong option. Inspect the actual destination page, not only the ingestion status.

## Keep retired items intentional

Decide how discontinued products leave the feed and what their links show. Do not reuse an old identifier for an unrelated new item solely to save setup work.

Preserve enough history to investigate a campaign or customer question about an earlier product. The mapping should explain the transition rather than conceal it.

## Connect the feed to the operating routine

Identify who updates the feed and how failures become visible. A manually refreshed feed should not be described as real-time synchronisation.

This is a preparation guide, not a claim that every feed destination is natively integrated with oBizee. Use the [catalogue and stock hub](/guides/catalogue-and-stock/) to make the underlying records consistent before using them in another system.

## Illustrative case to check

A blue medium shirt is renamed for a new collection. Its sellable identity should not accidentally become a different feed item solely because the title changed. Separately, a redesigned shirt with different construction should not inherit the old reference without a deliberate rule. Keep both decisions in the mapping so campaigns and product pages remain understandable.

title: Reconcile feed prices with the product and checkout
description: A feed price is useful only when it represents the product a buyer can actually choose. Compare the feed, landing page and checkout before sending more traffic to the offer.
body:
A feed price is useful only when it represents the product a buyer can actually choose. Compare the feed, landing page and checkout before sending more traffic to the offer.

## Choose an exact buying configuration

Specify the product, option and quantity. A starting price for a range cannot be compared fairly with the price of its most expensive variant. Keep currency and the treatment of delivery explicit.

Use a normal product, a sale item and a variant product as separate cases. One matching simple item does not prove the difficult paths.

## Record where the values originate

Identify the source for each displayed amount and how often it updates. If the feed is generated from a different export than the storefront, write down the timing difference.

Google's Merchant Center specification includes price and availability requirements. Confirm the current rules for the destination and the actual landing-page behaviour rather than assuming a technically accepted file is sufficient. [Product data specification](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/7052112?hl=en)

## Test a change through the whole path

In a controlled environment, change an allowed test value and observe the feed and page. Record when each reflects it. Do not advertise a sale ending at a precise time if the update routine cannot support that promise.

Include an unavailable product. A low price on an item that cannot be bought can waste customer attention even when the feed field is formatted correctly.

## Investigate differences before compensating

Do not manually change one surface solely to make a screenshot match. Find whether the discrepancy comes from variant selection, stale data, a discount rule or a different cost definition.

Keep the correction at the appropriate source. Otherwise the next export may restore the inconsistency.

## Make reconciliation repeatable

Use a short sample after pricing-policy changes and before important campaigns. Retain the tested item references, time and outcome. Give one person responsibility for following up on failures.

This guide does not promise a native feed integration or real-time synchronisation. Use the [pricing and platform hub](/guides/choosing-and-designing-store/) to define the offer first, then verify every representation of it.

## Illustrative case to check

A sale ends at midnight, but a manual feed is not refreshed until the next afternoon. A buyer may see the earlier offer before arriving at the new price. Identify the actual update gap and change the publishing routine or offer timing. Do not claim real-time consistency when the process depends on a later manual upload.

title: Keep unavailable products out of a careless retargeting promise
description: A visitor returning from an advertisement should find an offer the store can still explain and fulfil. Review availability and the destination before treating retargeting as an automatic recovery mechanism.
body:
A visitor returning from an advertisement should find an offer the store can still explain and fulfil. Review availability and the destination before treating retargeting as an automatic recovery mechanism.

## Define the item being promoted

A campaign may refer to a product family while the buyer previously viewed a specific option. Check whether the creative and link preserve that distinction.

If only another colour remains, do not imply the original choice is available. A relevant alternative can be presented honestly, but it should be recognisable as an alternative.

## Review the update path

Identify how product availability reaches the campaign system and how failures are detected. A scheduled export, manual upload and connected feed have different operating responsibilities.

Do not call the process live merely because it runs automatically sometimes. Write down the actual refresh routine and who checks rejected or stale records.

## Check the landing page after changes

Open the promoted link with the same context a customer receives. Inspect the item, price, option and availability message. A working homepage does not establish that an old product link remains useful.

Avoid sending unavailable products to an unrelated offer without explanation. The customer should understand what changed and what choices remain.

## Respect the audience boundary

Retargeting involves visitor data and advertising-platform rules. Confirm the applicable consent, privacy and audience requirements through the appropriate process before collecting or activating data.

This article is an operating checklist, not legal advice or a claim that every visitor can be contacted or matched. Do not upload customer information simply because a tool provides an import button.

## Judge outcomes beyond a recovered click

Track whether the returning visitor reaches an accurate product and can complete the intended next step. A high click count is not useful if the advertised option is repeatedly unavailable.

Use the [campaign budget calculator](/resources/campaign-budget/) with your own contribution assumptions, and read the [stock guides](/guides/catalogue-and-stock/) when the underlying issue is unreliable availability rather than advertising reach.

## Illustrative case to check

An advertisement shows a red bag, but only the black option remains. Pause or update the offer according to the campaign system's supported controls, and verify the destination. If you offer the black version as an alternative, say so. A customer should not need to discover the substitution only after clicking a product they thought was still available.

title: Keep a register of every custom script added to your store
description: A custom-code field can become an unowned collection of tags. Keep a register so every script has a purpose, an authorised owner and a way to be removed.
body:
A custom-code field can become an unowned collection of tags. Keep a register so every script has a purpose, an authorised owner and a way to be removed.

## Record the reason before pasting code

Name the service, the business question it supports and the pages where it needs to run. A script added because someone said it might improve tracking is not a complete requirement.

Identify whether an equivalent integration already exists. Duplicate installation can create confusing data or unnecessary work even when the page still appears normal.

## Know who supplied the code

Use the provider's current authorised instructions. Do not paste code from an unknown message or an old screenshot without checking its origin and purpose.

Keep secret credentials out of browser-delivered code. If an integration asks for a sensitive key in a public page, have the implementation reviewed before proceeding.

## Define the data boundary

List the information the integration may collect and the permissions or consent required for its use. Confirm the relevant requirements through the appropriate privacy process.

A useful register includes owner, installation location, purpose, data categories, date, test evidence and removal instructions. Store actual secrets elsewhere, not in the register.

## Test more than whether the tag appears

Check the storefront's important routes and the measurement outcome the script was meant to provide. Inspect failed and repeated actions where relevant. A tag loading is not proof that its event definitions are correct.

Also observe loading and interaction on a representative phone. If the change slows a buying step or breaks a control, the business value must be reconsidered.

## Remove deliberately

When a service is retired, confirm which script and related configuration can be removed. Keep a before-state and verify that unrelated integrations still work.

This guide does not claim that oBizee exposes a custom-head editor on every account. It describes the governance needed wherever such a capability exists. Use the [platform evaluation hub](/guides/choosing-and-designing-store/) to ask who owns these responsibilities before choosing an integration-heavy setup.

## Illustrative case to check

The store already sends a purchase event through one integration. A contractor proposes adding another snippet for the same provider. Check the existing installation and event ownership before proceeding. The register should make the potential duplicate visible, with a named person deciding whether the new snippet replaces, supplements or should not be added.

title: Evaluate a new store tag with a before-and-after test
description: A new analytics or marketing tag should answer a defined question without damaging the buying journey. Compare the same pages and tasks before and after installation.
body:
A new analytics or marketing tag should answer a defined question without damaging the buying journey. Compare the same pages and tasks before and after installation.

## Choose the important tasks first

Include opening a product, selecting an option, viewing the cart and reaching the relevant checkout stage. The homepage alone is a weak test of a commerce integration.

Use a representative mobile device and connection where practical. Record the conditions so an obviously faster network does not masquerade as an improvement.

## Preserve the before-state

Capture the existing configuration and note other changes scheduled for the same period. Avoid introducing several unrelated tags at once when you want to understand their effects.

Keep the test scope read-only unless an authorised test environment supports order or payment actions. A performance check should not accidentally generate real purchases.

## Verify the intended measurement

Write the expected event and business meaning. Confirm that a page reload, failed submission or cancelled flow does not become a successful outcome by mistake.

A script can have little visible performance effect while still reporting the wrong event. Conversely, an accurate event does not justify breaking a product control.

## Decide the rollback condition in advance

Define what would make you remove the change: a broken interaction, unacceptable loading regression, unexpected data collection or an event-counting error. Do not wait until launch pressure makes every failure seem tolerable.

The rollback should identify the exact configuration, not a broad instruction to delete all scripts.

## Keep the result with the owner

Record what passed, what remains uncertain and who will re-test after a checkout or theme change. One successful installation does not prove that future modifications preserve it.

This is a practical evaluation method, not a claim about a particular tag's current speed or compatibility. Read the [store design guides](/guides/choosing-and-designing-store/) to connect technical changes to the actual customer tasks you need to protect.

## Illustrative case to check

Before adding a chat widget, record the product and cart interactions on a representative phone. After installation, repeat those same tasks and verify the widget does not cover an important control. Also check the intended contact function. If it adds friction without producing the required support route, removing it can be the correct outcome.

title: Give an AI store assistant the smallest useful permission
description: An assistant that can read a catalogue does not automatically need permission to change prices, publish copy or alter orders. Separate advice from action when evaluating store automation.
body:
An assistant that can read a catalogue does not automatically need permission to change prices, publish copy or alter orders. Separate advice from action when evaluating store automation.

## List the job in plain language

Decide whether the tool should summarise information, draft a change, prepare a plan or execute an operation. Those are different permissions.

For example, identifying incomplete product descriptions may require reading public product data. Applying prices to every item is a separate action with a much larger consequence.

## Begin with read-only evidence

Ask the tool to show the records behind its recommendation. Check whether it understands a product option, an unavailable item and an older order correctly.

Do not grant broad write access merely because the summary sounds confident. A polished explanation can still rest on a misunderstood field.

## Define a bounded change

If action is useful, specify the exact records, permitted fields and maximum scope. Keep a before-state and a way to inspect the proposed difference.

A useful first test changes a controlled example, not the entire store. Avoid customer transactions or irreversible operations while establishing whether the assistant follows the boundary.

## Keep sensitive capabilities separate

Order deletion, payment configuration and customer-data access deserve particular care. Confirm the provider's permission model and current security documentation rather than assuming a conversational instruction replaces an access control.

Never paste credentials into the conversation as a shortcut. Use the supported secure connection process and understand how access can be revoked.

## Judge reliability by exceptions

Test what happens when data is missing, a request fails or the instruction conflicts with a store rule. The assistant should expose uncertainty rather than silently choose a broader action.

This is a selection framework, not a claim that oBizee includes a particular AI-agent integration. Use the [platform-choice guides](/guides/choosing-and-designing-store/) to compare responsibility and recovery alongside the appealing demonstration.

## Illustrative case to check

An assistant needs to identify missing product dimensions. Read access to the relevant public records may be enough. Permission to delete orders or change payment settings does not help that task. Begin with the narrow connection and inspect its findings. If you later authorise edits, scope them to the verified dimension fields and retain the previous values.

title: Prepare a minimal store dataset for an AI business question
description: An AI analysis does not need every customer detail simply because you can export it. Start with the business question and provide the smallest relevant dataset.
body:
An AI analysis does not need every customer detail simply because you can export it. Start with the business question and provide the smallest relevant dataset.

## Define the calculation or decision

Ask a concrete question, such as which products have incomplete descriptions or how contribution changes under an illustrative discount. A vague request to analyse everything encourages unnecessary collection and unfocused answers.

Write what a useful result should contain before preparing the file.

## Separate public product facts from private records

Product titles and public prices are different from customer addresses, payment references and internal notes. Do not combine them by default.

Where an aggregate answers the question, use it instead of individual customer records. Check the provider's current data-handling terms and your own obligations before uploading information.

## Explain the fields

A column named paid may have a particular application meaning. Define totals, refunds, delivery charges and time periods explicitly. Do not assume the tool will infer your accounting convention correctly.

Include a small data dictionary and mark missing values. A blank should not automatically become zero, especially when that changes the decision.

## Check a known example first

Choose one row or aggregate whose result you can calculate independently. Ask the tool to explain its arithmetic and treatment of missing information.

If it fails that example, fix the definitions before expanding the dataset. More rows will not repair a misunderstood field.

## Keep recommendations tied to evidence

Require the answer to separate observed facts, calculations and assumptions. A suggestion to raise prices is not justified merely because revenue rose in one period.

Retain the input version and the question so the result can be reproduced. Remove temporary files according to your authorised retention process, not an improvised promise that an upload has disappeared.

Use the [resources hub](/resources/) for transparent calculations that can be done locally without sending business records to another service. This guide does not imply a native AI analytics connection in oBizee.

## Illustrative case to check

To compare two discount scenarios, the tool may need product costs, prices and assumed quantities—not buyer names, addresses and phone numbers. Prepare that smaller table and define which costs are included. Calculate one row independently. If the assistant treats revenue as profit, correct the field definitions before accepting its recommendation.

title: Budget AI credits around a finished task rather than a demo
description: A credit allowance is hard to evaluate without knowing how much usable work it produces. Compare tools around a finished, checked task rather than the number in the plan headline.
body:
A credit allowance is hard to evaluate without knowing how much usable work it produces. Compare tools around a finished, checked task rather than the number in the plan headline.

## Define the unit of useful work

One generated paragraph is not necessarily one publishable product description. The task may also require fact checking, revision and formatting.

Choose a repeatable unit, such as ten accurate descriptions for existing products, and record what completion means. Include rejected outputs rather than counting only successful examples.

## Measure a small representative batch

Use ordinary products and a difficult one with options or missing information. Track the credits or billed usage shown by the provider and the time spent correcting the output.

Do not extrapolate from the easiest product alone. A catalogue containing many exceptions may have a different cost from a polished demonstration.

## Include the work outside the credit meter

Human checking, image rights, data preparation and integration maintenance can matter more than the generation charge. Keep those costs visible when comparing plans.

An illustrative comparison might separate subscription cost, variable usage and review time. Use your actual quoted prices; this guide supplies no current vendor price list.

## Check expiry and overage terms

Read the provider's current rules for renewal, unused credits, extra usage and cancellation. A headline allowance does not explain all of those conditions.

Avoid assuming that two services define a credit identically. Compare the observed cost of your task, not the nominal unit count.

## Set a stopping rule

Decide when a batch should stop because quality is inadequate or usage is exceeding the planned limit. A tool should not keep consuming resources simply because it has more products to process.

Use the [plan-cost calculator](/resources/plan-cost/) for the fixed commitment and retain the sample evidence behind your variable-cost estimate. The best choice is the one that completes your actual work reliably, not the one whose credit number looks largest.

## Illustrative case to check

A sample batch creates ten descriptions, but three need complete rewriting and two need factual corrections. Count the entire usage and review effort required to reach ten usable outputs. Do not divide the charge only by the five easy successes and call that the normal cost. Keep the difficult products in the next evaluation batch.

title: Write stop conditions for an automated store task
description: An automation needs a definition of when not to continue. Write stop conditions before it touches a large catalogue or a live business record.
body:
An automation needs a definition of when not to continue. Write stop conditions before it touches a large catalogue or a live business record.

## Name the intended result

Specify the records, fields and outcome. “Improve the store” is not a bounded task. “Prepare draft descriptions for these ten products using these verified facts” is easier to inspect.

State whether the result is a draft or a live change. The tool should not infer publication authority from permission to write text.

## Identify the uncertain cases

Missing prices, conflicting product facts, unavailable images and unknown option combinations should have an explicit treatment. The safest useful result may be a flagged row rather than a guessed value.

Do not turn a blank into a confident claim solely to keep the batch moving.

## Set operational limits

Choose a maximum batch size, time or spend appropriate to the task. Decide what happens after repeated errors or an unexpected response.

The limit is a guardrail, not a quality metric. Finishing within budget does not prove that the output is correct.

## Preserve a recoverable before-state

For permitted changes, keep the original values and a record of what was applied. Confirm how rollback works before assuming every action can be reversed.

A content edit and an order or payment operation have different consequences. Do not use one generic undo promise for both.

## Test the refusal path

Create a safe example with missing or contradictory information and confirm that the automation stops or flags it as designed. A happy-path demonstration cannot prove the boundary.

Record the exception and who resolves it. This allows the rest of a safe batch to proceed without hiding the unresolved case.

Use the [help library](/help/) to understand the actual application action before automating around it. This guide is a process design, not a claim that a conversational instruction alone enforces technical permissions or makes an integration safe.

## Illustrative case to check

A batch is authorised to draft descriptions for 20 identified products. One record has no confirmed material. The automation should flag that item and continue only with safe, permitted work, not infer cotton from the photograph. Its result should distinguish completed drafts from unresolved ones rather than report 20 successes.

title: Build a product fact pack before asking AI for a launch campaign
description: A launch campaign can only remain accurate if every asset starts from the same product facts. Prepare that source before generating captions, images or advertising variations.
body:
A launch campaign can only remain accurate if every asset starts from the same product facts. Prepare that source before generating captions, images or advertising variations.

## Write the facts that must not drift

Include the product identity, material, dimensions, options, price, availability and genuine delivery expectation. Mark what is unknown rather than letting a tool fill it.

Keep approved photographs separate from inspiration images. A visual reference is not permission to present another maker's work as your product.

## Define the offer once

Record the actual offer and its limits. If there is no discount, say so. If a deadline depends on stock or production capacity, explain that boundary.

The campaign should not invent urgency, a crossed-out price or a shipping promise because those patterns are common in advertisements.

## Add the questions customers ask

Use genuine recurring questions where you have them. Otherwise label proposed questions as hypotheses, not customer research.

A helpful launch asset may answer size, included pieces or care rather than shouting that the item is new. Choose the information according to the buying decision.

## Generate variations around one stable promise

Ask for different presentations of the same verified facts. Keep a register connecting each asset to the product and offer version.

Review the caption, image and landing page together. An accurate caption cannot rescue a picture that shows the wrong accessory, and a correct image cannot rescue a stale price.

## Check the operational handoff

Confirm the product link and available option before publishing through your normal process. Decide how you will handle enquiries that the campaign creates.

This guide does not claim that oBizee automatically generates or publishes a complete campaign. It describes the preparation that makes any drafting tool more useful.

Use the [catalogue guides](/guides/catalogue-and-stock/) to complete the fact pack and the [selling hub](/guides/selling-online/) to choose the next action for the audience. A campaign is ready when its promise matches the store, not when it contains the largest number of assets.

## Illustrative case to check

A launch pack says a keychain is sold singly, while an old photo shows three. The generated creative must not imply a three-piece offer unless that is what the product supplies. Add an explicit included-item statement, choose an accurate image treatment and verify the landing page before publishing any variant of the campaign.

title: Review a batch of AI product copy for factual drift
description: Checking one generated description is not enough to establish that a whole batch is accurate. Review the claims most likely to change the customer's decision.
body:
Checking one generated description is not enough to establish that a whole batch is accurate. Review the claims most likely to change the customer's decision.

## Create a claim checklist

List materials, dimensions, included items, prices, availability, care instructions and delivery statements. Add any category-specific claims that require evidence.

For jewellery, that may include metal or stone descriptions. For clothing, it may include fit and fabric. The checklist should follow the product rather than a generic writing score.

## Compare against the approved source

Keep each output connected to its product reference and fact pack. Do not compare only against another AI-generated summary.

When a fact is missing, the output should remain appropriately limited. Words such as premium, sustainable or guaranteed are not harmless decoration if they imply unsupported qualities.

## Look for systematic errors

A repeated mistake may come from the prompt or data mapping. If every variant description uses the parent price, correct the cause before editing dozens of outputs individually.

Group failures by type: invented claim, omitted distinction, wrong product, stale offer or confusing instruction. That makes the next batch more reliable.

## Keep the customer's task central

A description can be factually safe but still unhelpful. Check whether the reader can understand what arrives, choose an option and know what happens next.

Do not pad every page to the same length simply to make the batch look substantial. Add detail where it resolves a real buying question.

## Retain the disposition

Mark each item accepted, revised or held, with the reason for held content. Do not count a generated file as a finished page while its central facts remain uncertain.

Use the [product-catalogue overview](/features/product-catalogue/) to organise the records behind the copy. This is a quality-control routine for drafts, not proof that an AI tool has independently verified a merchant's products.

## Illustrative case to check
