In a batch of jewellery copy, several outputs add “hypoallergenic” even though the source only says stainless steel. Treat that as a systematic unsupported claim. Correct the instructions and review every affected output rather than fixing one example. The absence of a complaint is not evidence that the material claim was verified.

title: Check an AI ad creative against the offer on the landing page
description: An advertisement and its destination should make the same offer. Check them together before publishing a generated creative, especially when price or availability appears in the image.
body:
An advertisement and its destination should make the same offer. Check them together before publishing a generated creative, especially when price or availability appears in the image.

## Identify the exact product

Record the product and option shown. A generated image can make a variation appear different from the item the store supplies.

Use genuine product evidence to check colour, shape, included pieces and scale. Do not accept a visually attractive alteration that changes what the customer believes they will receive.

## Compare every offer element

Check the price, discount wording, delivery statement and deadline against the landing page. Include small text and badges, not only the main caption.

An offer can become inconsistent when one surface is updated and another is not. Keep the asset's source version and review date so outdated creatives can be identified.

## Make the next action specific

The link should help the customer reach the advertised choice. A broad store homepage may not be the best destination for a narrowly described item.

Open the link on a phone and verify that the product is available, the option can be selected and the promised information is visible.

## Test one meaningful difference

If comparing creative variants, keep the underlying offer stable enough to understand what changed. Altering the product, price, image and audience simultaneously makes the result difficult to interpret.

Use a spending limit based on your own contribution and risk tolerance. This guide does not prescribe a daily ad budget or guarantee a return.

## Plan the end of the offer

Decide who removes or updates the creative when stock, price or timing changes. Automation that creates an asset does not automatically maintain its truth later.

Use the [campaign-budget resource](/resources/campaign-budget/) and [selling guides](/guides/selling-online/) to connect the creative to a real operating plan. A correct promise is more important than a dramatic generated visual.

## Illustrative case to check

The creative says ₹499, the product page says ₹549 and checkout includes an additional delivery charge. Resolve the actual offer and explain applicable charges before publishing. Do not simply choose the lowest number for every surface. The acceptance check should compare the same product configuration and distinguish item price from the final payable amount.

title: Separate an AI sales recommendation from a forecast you can defend
description: An AI tool can suggest a next action without proving what the action will earn. Keep observations, assumptions and forecasts separate before changing prices or spending.
body:
An AI tool can suggest a next action without proving what the action will earn. Keep observations, assumptions and forecasts separate before changing prices or spending.

## Ask what the recommendation is based on

Require the relevant time period, product group and calculation. A statement that one item is growing may reflect a small base, a promotion or a stock change.

Do not accept a confident conclusion if the tool cannot identify the data behind it.

## Distinguish revenue from contribution

More sales are not automatically more useful if the offer leaves little after product, packing, payment and delivery costs. Define the cost boundary before asking for an expansion plan.

Use the [margin calculator](/resources/margin/) with your actual inputs to make the arithmetic visible. It does not predict demand.

## Turn the suggestion into a scenario

Write the proposed action and the assumptions required for it to work. For example, an advertising increase may assume enough stock, a stable conversion rate and an acceptable acquisition cost.

Run a conservative case rather than relying on a single expected outcome. If the recommendation only works under optimistic assumptions, treat that as a decision constraint.

## Check what the model cannot observe

Customer intent, future demand, supplier reliability and competitor changes may not be in the dataset. The tool should not convert missing information into certainty.

Likewise, a correlation between a campaign and orders does not by itself establish causation. Ask what else changed during the period.

## Choose a bounded test

Define the spending or operational limit, the measurement and the stopping condition. Keep a record of the result so the next recommendation can be compared with reality.

This is a decision framework, not personalised financial advice or a promise about an AI product. Use [pricing decision guides](/guides/choosing-and-designing-store/) to examine the trade-off before letting a generated forecast become a live business commitment.

## Illustrative case to check

A tool predicts that doubling advertising spend doubles orders. Ask which evidence supports a constant acquisition cost and whether stock and fulfilment capacity can support the result. Turn it into an explicit scenario, not a forecast presented as fact. Set a limited test and preserve the assumptions so the outcome can be interpreted later.

title: Turn a PDF catalogue into product records without trusting every extracted number
description: A PDF catalogue can be a useful starting source, but extracted text still needs to be matched to the right product. Treat uncertain prices and options as review items, not automatically publishable data.
body:
A PDF catalogue can be a useful starting source, but extracted text still needs to be matched to the right product. Treat uncertain prices and options as review items, not automatically publishable data.

## Preserve the original document

Keep the source PDF and its date so every extracted field can be checked. Work on a separate transformation file.

Confirm that you have permission to use the product information and images. A supplier document is not automatically a licence to republish every asset.

## Define the destination fields

List the title, description, price, options, category and image references required by the destination. Mark fields the PDF does not contain.

Do not turn a visually grouped table into separate products without understanding its meaning. A column may describe sizes, pack quantities or wholesale tiers rather than independent retail items.

## Inspect difficult extraction cases

Check decimal points, currency symbols, crossed-out prices, footnotes and text placed beside several images. A number can be correctly extracted but assigned to the wrong item.

Use explicit uncertainty flags. An unreadable amount should not become zero or a guessed price just to satisfy an import format.

## Reconcile at product level

Compare the source entry with the transformed record and intended photograph. Count products separately from variants and image files.

Start with a small private sample and inspect the rendered result before preparing the full import. Do not publish the sample to customers without the appropriate release process.

## Keep corrections reproducible

Record what was manually changed and why. If the source PDF is updated, those decisions should not be lost in an unexplained spreadsheet.

This guide does not claim that oBizee has a PDF importer. Confirm the available tool and format before preparing a live upload. Use the [catalogue help](/help/first-product/) to understand the current product fields and the [catalogue hub](/guides/catalogue-and-stock/) to improve the source information first.

## Illustrative case to check

A PDF table lists “12” beside a product and “₹600” in a shared column. Determine whether 12 means pieces per pack, a minimum quantity or a model number before importing. A correct text extraction can still produce the wrong selling unit. Hold the row until the catalogue owner confirms its meaning.

title: Convert social posts into a catalogue without reviving old offers
description: An old social post can contain a useful product photograph and an offer that is no longer true. Separate reusable product facts from time-specific promotion before building a catalogue record.
body:
An old social post can contain a useful product photograph and an offer that is no longer true. Separate reusable product facts from time-specific promotion before building a catalogue record.

## Establish that the item is still sold

Check the product with the merchant's current records. A post remaining online does not mean the item, colour or price remains available.

Mark discontinued or uncertain entries instead of importing everything into an active store.

## Separate description from promotion

Keep genuine material, size and included-item information where it is still accurate. Remove expired deadlines, temporary discounts and old delivery claims unless they remain intentionally valid.

Do not infer a permanent product name from a campaign slogan. Give the catalogue a stable identity that can be understood without the original post.

## Verify image rights and accuracy

Confirm the business is entitled to reuse the image and that it still depicts the item being sold. A customer photograph or collaboration asset may have a different permission boundary from the merchant's own product photo.

Do not crop away an important qualification or generate a replacement that changes the product.

## Rebuild the buying information

Social copy may omit options, stock and fulfilment details because the original workflow expected a conversation. Fill those fields from current evidence, not from inference.

Ask the merchant to resolve missing facts. A draft with a clear unresolved field is safer than a complete-looking listing containing invented details.

## Keep a source trail

Record the original post reference, current product identity and the date the facts were checked. That helps explain later differences without treating the old caption as the permanent source of truth.

This is a preparation method, not a claim of automatic Instagram catalogue import. Use [product-catalogue guidance](/features/product-catalogue/) to shape the destination record and [social-selling guides](/guides/selling-online/) to decide how the refreshed catalogue should be shared.

## Illustrative case to check

An old post advertises a festive set with free delivery until a date that has passed. The photographs may still be usable with permission, but the offer is not automatically current. Confirm the product composition and current price, then create a fresh catalogue record without carrying over the expired delivery claim.

title: Deduplicate catalogue imports using identity rather than similar names
description: Two similar names can describe different products, while two different names can describe the same item. Define a product-identity rule before merging imported records.
body:
Two similar names can describe different products, while two different names can describe the same item. Define a product-identity rule before merging imported records.

## Choose the strongest available reference

Use a stable SKU or product reference where one exists, then check whether it genuinely identifies the sellable item. Do not assume a supplier code is unique across every source.

Document the role of variant references separately. A size or colour combination may need its own identity even when it belongs to one parent product.

## Separate exact matches from possible matches

An exact reference match can be handled differently from a fuzzy title match. Keep uncertain pairs in a review group instead of automatically collapsing them.

Compare material, dimensions, options and source before deciding. A newer product version may look similar while needing to remain distinct.

## Decide what survives a merge

Specify which record supplies the title, images, price and category. Do not simply keep whichever row appeared last in a file.

Also consider links, reviews and order references. A catalogue clean-up should not silently break the identity used by another business record.

## Test reruns before a full import

Ask how the tool handles an already imported record. A second upload might update, duplicate or reject it depending on the implementation.

Use a controlled sample to establish that behaviour. Keep the import result and the mapping rather than assuming a button labelled import is idempotent.

## Reconcile the outcome

Count new, updated, held and rejected records separately. A lower row count after deduplication is not proof that every merge was correct.

Keep the original export untouched and maintain a reason for manual decisions. This guide does not claim a particular import capability in oBizee.

Use the [catalogue and stock library](/guides/catalogue-and-stock/) to stabilise your product structure before moving data. Good identity rules reduce repeated cleanup more effectively than increasingly aggressive title matching.

## Illustrative case to check

Two rows share “Sunflower keychain,” but one is a single item and the other is a pack of five. A title-only merge would destroy a meaningful difference. Compare the selling unit and stable reference before merging. Keep a possible-match queue for ambiguous rows instead of raising the matching threshold until they disappear.

title: Check data portability before connecting another store automation tool
description: A useful automation should not leave you unable to retrieve the records needed to continue your business. Evaluate export and disconnection alongside the demonstration.
body:
A useful automation should not leave you unable to retrieve the records needed to continue your business. Evaluate export and disconnection alongside the demonstration.

## List the data the tool will create

Separate original store records from generated descriptions, image assets, campaign plans and activity logs. Ask which system becomes the authoritative source for each.

If the tool edits existing records, identify whether the original values and change history remain accessible.

## Request a real export example

Inspect a supported export format with a safe sample. Check whether identifiers, timestamps and relationships are preserved, not only whether a file downloads.

A text dump may be readable but difficult to use for a future migration. An image export may omit the information connecting each asset to its product.

## Examine the disconnection process

Ask how access is revoked and what happens to scheduled work, stored copies and published changes. Use the provider's current terms and controls rather than relying on an informal reassurance.

Do not disconnect a live integration experimentally without understanding its dependencies. Plan the test in a controlled setting.

## Keep sensitive data out of unnecessary exports

Portability does not require copying every customer detail into every tool. Retrieve only what the legitimate task needs and handle it under the appropriate access and retention rules.

Keep account credentials separate from exported business content.

## Make the exit cost part of the decision

Record the effort required to continue without the tool. A low subscription price can be less attractive if important records cannot be recovered in a usable form.

This guide is not a claim about any vendor's current export entitlement. It is a checklist for verifying the plan and integration you are considering.

Use the [platform comparison library](/guides/choosing-and-designing-store/) to compare ownership and recovery with features. A good demonstration shows how the tool helps; a good evaluation also shows how the business continues when the tool is no longer used.

## Illustrative case to check

An assistant stores revised product copy in its own workspace while only the final text reaches the shop. Before subscribing, inspect whether you can export the copy with product references and change history. If the export is just an unlabelled text file, include the manual reconstruction effort in your decision.
